title: Getting Started with geneRosetta
text: Comparing gene lists across studies (especially older ones) can frustrating. Gene symbols change, IDs deprecated, different databases sometimes disagree. makes hard compare results across studies, even reproduce analysis months. geneRosetta solves problem building multi-source reference uses map gene symbols IDs. package combines several sources: Combining sources helps recover aliases records missing one database. Unlike packages static, outdated reference data — need live server connection every lookup, can fail middle analysis — downloads references every source real-time, merges , caches merged reference locally. completely offline? problem - use built-cached data. Need update reference? Refresh using recently available data. Furthermore, geneRosetta designed forgive real-world messy inputs: automatically trims surrounding whitespace, ignores case differences, strips version numbers Ensembl IDs (e.g., converting ENSG00000141510.5 ENSG00000141510). Species Note Choose species matches experiment. functions map identifiers within species; find equivalent orthologs across species.

title: Getting Started with geneRosetta
text: , face big problem frequent gene symbol changes. Nomenclature changes whenever scientific community discovers new function - - whenever Excel decides gene name looks suspiciously like calendar date. mapping performed two phases (passes): Exact Match: Matching input symbol provided. Alias Search: Searching input known gene synonyms historical aliases. example, although p53 widely used gene symbol Tumor Protein P53, official symbol TP53. p53 searched strict official database, match. second pass, symbol “rescued”. Another challenge one symbol can sometimes map multiple gene IDs. case, choose strategy via multi_handling: keepAll: one row per match (mappings preserved; may expand rows) collapse: one row per input, values joined | (cleaner table; prevents row expansion) unique: keep one mapping (first sorted match; prevents row expansion) multi_handling = "unique" used symbol mapping, prioritizes records non-missing ensembl_id sorts ensembl_id. Multi-mapping typically two distinct biological causes: Genuinely distinct loci — example CD99, sits pseudoautosomal region (PAR) separate functional IDs X Y chromosomes. Alternate haplotype copies — genes HLA-appear primary assembly (chromosome 6) alternative haplotype scaffold (e.g., chr6(GL000256.2)). chromosome values carry chr6(...) form, making easy spot filter . example, include: " p53 ": gene whose name updated (TP53), leading/trailing spaces test whitespace trimming INS: standard gene symbol CD99: gene multiple Ensembl IDs X & Y FAKEGENE: intentionally invalid gene symbol Console output summarizes happened. returned list object contains: Input symbols stored query_gene_symbol, current official symbols gene_symbol (showing updates like p53 → TP53). can include extra metadata (NCBI + naming authority IDs, biotype, genomic coordinates, description) add_metadata = TRUE (default): CD99 maps multiple Ensembl IDs, keepAll prints one row per match. Use multi_handling = "collapse" one-row summaries: Now multiple values joined | single row. Note Collapsed Columns multi_handling = "collapse" used, column collapsed independently. strict row--row linkage IDs coordinates required, keep multi_handling = "keepAll". default, unmapped genes omitted mapped table (always accessible id_lookup$unmapped_final). Set keep_unmapped = TRUE keep output table NA values: can also pass full dataframe (differential expression results) specify symbol column using col_id. handy table already contains statistics (example, gene expression results) want results annotation data one step. Tips Annotating Dataframes Handling Name Collisions: input dataframe already columns names annotation (ensembl_id, gene_biotype, chromosome, gene_start, gene_end, strand, gene_description), query_ prefix automatically added original column names, can compare old new values. Tracking Expanded Rows: choose multi_handling = "keepAll" dataframe, multi-mapped genes expand multiple rows. optional row observation ID table can make easier trace expanded rows back avoid overcounting measurements downstream enrichment tests. mapIDToSymbol() accepts vector dataframe column Ensembl gene IDs NCBI Gene (Entrez) IDs auto-detects ID type. Key details know ID mapping: Single-Pass: Unlike symbol mapping (alias rescue pass), ID mapping single-pass lookup. Suffix & Space Trimming: Version numbers Ensembl IDs (e.g., .5 ENSG00000141510.5) automatically stripped, leading/trailing whitespace removed. Default Output: Like mapSymbolToID(), keep_unmapped = FALSE default. Set keep_unmapped = TRUE wish retain unmapped IDs output table. example, include mix versioned, whitespace, multi-mapped, unmapped IDs: "ENSG00000141510.5": versioned Ensembl ID (TP53) " ensg00000012048 ": Ensembl ID whitespace lowercase formatting (BRCA1) "ENSG00000226087": multi-mapped Ensembl ID (maps LOC105374588 LOC124907763) "ENSG00000000000": non-existent/unmapped Ensembl ID Like mapSymbolToID(), returned object carries mapped table diagnostic diagnostics: input number/numeric vector, assumed represent NCBI / Entrez IDs.
